title: Designing Strongly Correlated Quantum Phases of Matter with Foundation Neural-Network Quantum States
authors: Alessandro Sinibaldi, Luciano Loris Viteritti, Riccardo Rende, Federico Becca, Giuseppe Carleo
abstract: Designing a material with a desired property amounts to solving an inverse problem: finding the couplings of a microscopic Hamiltonian whose ground state exhibits that property. For strongly correlated quantum systems, solving this problem efficiently remains largely out of reach. To address this challenge, we present a general framework for ab initio inverse design based on Foundation Neural-Network Quantum States, a recent approach in which the ground states of a family of Hamiltonians are encoded in a single variational wave function. Because the ansatz depends explicitly on the couplings, any target property is a differentiable function of them, and the search for the right Hamiltonian reduces to gradient-based optimization in coupling space. We apply this approach to search for nonmagnetic phases of frustrated Heisenberg models on the square lattice with an increasing number of free next-nearest-neighbor couplings, aiming to identify new quantum spin liquid candidates. With a single coupling, the method recovers the known nonmagnetic window of the square $J_1$-$J_2$ Heisenberg model, whereas letting the two diagonal couplings vary independently reveals an extended nonmagnetic region connecting the square-lattice and anisotropic-triangular-lattice regimes. In a search space of eight independent couplings within a $2\times2$ unit cell, which contains several paradigmatic frustrated spin models, the optimization spontaneously converges to the $J_1$-$J_2$-$δ$ Heisenberg model, in which the diagonal couplings alternate between two values on neighboring plaquettes, a model recently proposed in the context of altermagnetism. Finite-size scaling up to $16\times16$ clusters in this optimal model shows that the ground state has no magnetic, dimer, or plaquette order, establishing it as a new quantum spin liquid candidate, distinct from those previously proposed on the square lattice.
summary: This work introduces a novel inverse design framework using Foundation Neural-Network Quantum States (FNQS) to solve the challenge of finding Hamiltonians that realize specific quantum properties. By treating the Hamiltonian couplings as optimization variables, the authors successfully located a new quantum spin liquid candidate in the frustrated Heisenberg model. This method represents a significant advance in computationally exploring the phase diagrams of strongly correlated materials.
main_problem: The core problem is solving the inverse design problem: determining the microscopic Hamiltonian couplings required for a quantum system to exhibit a desired target property.
main_result: The authors successfully used their framework to find a novel quantum spin liquid candidate—the J1-J2-delta model—by optimizing couplings in a search space of eight parameters.
method: They employ a general framework using Foundation Neural-Network Quantum States (FNQS) to encode the ground states of a family of Hamiltonians. The search is reduced to gradient-based optimization in the coupling space, minimizing a target observable.
model_or_system: The study focuses on strongly correlated quantum spin systems, specifically frustrated Heisenberg models on the square lattice, parameterized by various couplings (e.g., J1, J2, and diagonal couplings).
key_observables: The primary target observable for finding QSL candidates is the Edwards-Anderson order parameter ($Q_2$), which must approach zero in the thermodynamic limit.
important_parameters: The search space involves up to eight independent couplings within a $2	imes2$ unit cell, and the analysis involves finite-size scaling up to $16	imes16$ clusters.
main_assumptions: The optimization is constrained by the variational nature of the state, and the method relies on the assumption that the target property is a differentiable function of the couplings.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the iterative FNQS Inverse Model Design framework, showing the cycle of local state training followed by gradient-based coupling updates.
paper_structure: The paper outlines the inverse design framework, detailing the use of FNQS to parameterize the Hamiltonian couplings. It then applies this framework to search for nonmagnetic phases in frustrated Heisenberg models, demonstrating convergence to a specific, previously uncharacterized model.
why_interesting: The methodology provides a powerful, automated way to explore the vast parameter space of frustrated quantum magnets, potentially discovering new exotic phases without relying on prior physical intuition about the Hamiltonian structure.
